seo.description: HAART is a volunteer-run, foster-based, no-kill animal rescue in Perth, Western Australia, founded in 2012.

sections.heading: A rescue with no shelter, on purpose
sections.lead: A group of like-minded individuals came together from other rescues with the idea of doing things different. From this we have grown to the rescue we are today.

children.text: HAART is a Not-For-Profit Charitable organisation that saves the lives of hundreds of animals each year, supported only by the generosity of the general public for our funding.

We don't have a premises with hundreds of animals awaiting adoption. Instead, we have a team of dedicated foster carers – people just like yourselves – who take scared, abused, and unwanted animals into their homes, give them the gift of life, and love them like their own, until we find them the perfect forever home.
HAART is exclusively no-kill and do not put animals to sleep just because they don't have room.
Our goal is to see the day when we are no longer needed. We would like nothing more than to put ourselves out of a job, because that would mean there are no more homeless animals.

steps.heading: An animal comes to us
steps.text: From a council pound where its time has run out, or from an owner who can no longer keep it. We take on what we have foster places for, and we never put an animal to sleep for want of space.

steps.heading: A vet sees it first
steps.text: Every animal is checked, vaccinated, microchipped and desexed before adoption. Injuries and illness are treated before anything else happens.

steps.heading: It goes to a foster home
steps.text: Living in a real home tells us what a kennel never could: how the animal is with children, cats, other dogs, being left alone, car trips, the vacuum cleaner.

steps.heading: We match it to a family
steps.text: Adopters complete a questionnaire, we talk, and we visit. Then the foster carer and the adopter meet. The foster carer knows the animal best, so their word counts.

items.heading: Free desexing for accidental litters
items.text: If you surrender an accidental litter to us for rehoming, we desex the parents at no cost so it does not happen again.

items.heading: Community education
items.text: We advance public knowledge of sterilisation, microchipping, vaccination, socialisation and training, because fewer animals in pounds is the whole point.

items.heading: Working with pounds and other rescues
items.text: Rescue is a network. We take animals from council pounds across Perth and work alongside other groups rather than in competition with them.

seo.description: Adopt a rescue dog or cat in Perth through HAART. Every animal is vet checked, desexed, vaccinated and microchipped, and assessed in a foster home.

sections.heading: Adopt a dog or cat
sections.lead: HAART dreams of a world where every companion animal is in a loving, caring and secure home, and by adopting, you could be part of this vision.

sections.heading: Who are you looking for?
sections.dogsText: Puppies to seniors, assessed in foster homes across Perth.
sections.catsText: Kittens and adult cats, all desexed and ready for an indoor life.

sections.heading: How adoption works
sections.intro: Four steps, usually a week or two from start to finish.

steps.heading: Tell us about your home
steps.text: Complete the pre-adoption questionnaire for dogs or cats. It asks about your household, your yard or unit, and your routine. It is not a test; it helps us match you well.

steps.heading: We call you
steps.text: Within seven days a volunteer will call to talk through your answers and the animals that might suit.

steps.heading: Meet and greet, and a home check
steps.text: You meet the animal with its foster carer, who knows it best. A volunteer visits your home to check that the yard and fencing are suitable, because the safety of our animals comes first.

steps.heading: Adoption day
steps.text: Sign the adoption agreement, pay the fee, and take your new family member home. The foster carer stays a phone call away for the first few weeks.

sections.heading: Adoption fees
sections.inclusions: All adoption fees include microchipping and sterilisation as well as up to date vaccinations, flea treatment and worming. Adopting two animals together? Ask us about a reduced fee.

items.question: I rent. Can I adopt?
items.answer: Yes, with your landlord's written permission for the type of animal. The questionnaire asks for it.

items.question: Can I meet an animal before applying?
items.answer: We ask for the questionnaire first. It takes ten minutes and means the foster carer's time goes to people who are ready to adopt. Meet and greets are arranged after the call.

items.question: What if it does not work out?
items.answer: Tell us straight away. Every HAART animal comes back to HAART, for life. We would far rather rehome carefully a second time than have an animal end up in a pound.

items.question: Do you adopt outside Perth?
items.answer: Occasionally, for the right match, if a home check can be arranged. Ask when we call.

sections.heading: Ready to apply?
sections.text: The questionnaire is the first step for every adoption.

seo.description: Become a foster carer with HAART in Perth. We cover vet costs and support you; you provide the home. Short and long-term fostering for dogs and cats.

sections.heading: Foster carers are the rescue
sections.lead: By welcoming an animal into your home you are saving them from the streets, the pound or potentially being put to sleep. Fostering an animal before they are adopted allows us to learn their temperament and needs so that we can find them the perfect forever home.

children.text: HAART has a team of dedicated foster carers – people just like yourselves – who take scared, abused, and unwanted animals into their homes, give them the gift of life, and love them like their own, until we find them the perfect forever home.
The main requirements for a potential foster carer are that they can provide a warm bed, a full belly, patience and lots of love.
Without foster homes we cannot take an animal out of the pound. Every new carer is, quite literally, another life we can say yes to.

sections.heading: What fostering actually involves
sections.intro: The honest version. Details to confirm with the foster coordinator are marked on the application.

items.heading: Vet costs are covered
items.text: HAART pays for veterinary treatment arranged through our vets. You never pay a vet bill for a foster animal.

items.heading: Help with supplies
items.text: Food, a bed, a crate or a lead can be provided if you need them. Many carers use their own; either is fine.

items.heading: Usually two to eight weeks
items.text: Puppies and kittens move fast. Adult dogs with a bit of history take longer. You tell us what you can manage and we match to that.

items.heading: Some driving
items.text: Vet visits and meet and greets are on you, with our transport volunteers as backup when you are stuck.

items.heading: A coordinator on the end of the phone
items.text: A foster coordinator checks in, answers the 9 pm questions, and steps in if something is not working.

items.heading: Letting go
items.text: Yes, you will get attached. Handing an animal to a family you have helped choose is the best part, and there is always another one waiting.

items.question: I work full time.
items.answer: Plenty of our carers do. We match you with an animal that copes with a working household, and puppies and animals on medication go to carers who are home more.

items.question: I have my own dog or cat.
items.answer: Good. A settled resident animal often helps a foster settle. We introduce carefully and only place animals we know are social with others.

items.question: I rent.
items.answer: Fostering is temporary, but you still need your landlord's permission for animals. The application asks for it.

items.question: What if it does not work out?
items.answer: Ring the coordinator. We move the animal to another carer, no judgement. It happens, and it is always better to say so early.

items.question: What if I want to adopt my foster?
items.answer: It happens so often it has a name. Tell the coordinator before the animal is listed and you go through the normal adoption steps.

items.question: Do I need a fenced yard?
items.answer: For most dogs, yes, and secure. For cats, an indoor home with screens on windows. Small dogs and puppies can suit units with a plan for toileting.

seo.description: Volunteer with HAART in Perth: transport, events, photography, home checks, fundraising and admin.

sections.heading: Help without fostering
sections.lead: HAART receives no government funding and is run entirely by a small group of volunteers. Most jobs take a few hours a month and none of them need experience.

items.heading: Transport
items.text: Pound pick-ups, vet runs and moving animals between foster homes. A car, a crate and a free morning.

items.heading: Events and stalls
items.text: Adoption days, quiz nights, sausage sizzles and Christmas photos. Set up, talk to people, pack down.

items.heading: Home checks
items.text: Visit prospective adopters and foster carers to check the yard and the fence. We show you what to look for.

items.heading: Photography and stories
items.text: Good photos get animals adopted. If you can take one, or write two hundred words about a foster, we need you.

items.heading: Fundraising
items.text: Run the auction, ask a business for a raffle prize, organise a workplace fundraiser.

items.heading: Admin
items.text: Answering the inbox, following up applications, keeping the animal listings current.

items.question: How much time?
items.answer: Whatever you say on the form. Some people do one event a year. Some do a vet run every week.

items.question: Is there training?
items.answer: For home checks and transport, yes, and you go out with an experienced volunteer first.

items.question: Can I volunteer with my kids?
items.answer: Events and stalls, yes. Transport and home checks are adults only.

seo.description: Thinking about surrendering a dog or cat in Perth? What HAART can take on, and what to do first.

sections.heading: Surrendering an animal
sections.lead: Sometimes keeping an animal is not possible. Here is how we can help, and what we need from you.

children.text: HAART rehomes private surrenders as well as pound animals, but we can only take on what we have a foster place for. Please contact us before you make any decision, and please do not leave an animal at a pound if there is any other option.
If you have an accidental litter, we can take the puppies or kittens for responsible rehoming, desexed, and we will desex the parents at no cost to you.
What we will ask: the animal's age, vet history, temperament with people and other animals, and the reason for surrender. Being honest about behaviour is what keeps the animal safe in its next home.
Details of the surrender process are being confirmed with the committee. Until then, email or call and a volunteer will talk it through.

items.question: Is there a surrender fee?
items.answer: To be confirmed. Where there is one, it goes toward the vet work the animal needs before adoption.

items.question: Will I hear how the animal goes?
items.answer: If you would like to, yes, once it is adopted.

items.question: Can you take my animal today?
items.answer: Rarely. We need a foster place first. In an emergency, call us and your local council ranger.

seo.description: How HAART collects, uses and protects personal information.

sections.heading: Privacy policy
sections.lead: Draft for adoption by the committee. Written for the Australian Privacy Principles.

children.text: Who we are

Homeless And Abused Animal Rescue Team Association Inc (HAART, we, us) is a volunteer-run animal rescue based in Perth, Western Australia. This policy explains what personal information we collect through haart.org.au and what we do with it.
What we collect

When you complete a form on this site (adoption questionnaire, foster application, volunteer registration, contact or partnership enquiry) we collect the details you enter: your name, contact details, and information about your home and household that helps us place animals safely. When you donate through our payment provider, the provider collects your payment details; we receive your name, email address, the amount and the date. When you buy merchandise, Square processes the order.
How we use it

To respond to you, to assess adoption and foster applications, to arrange home checks and meet and greets, to issue receipts, and to contact you about the animal you enquired about. If you tick the newsletter box or sign up on our newsletter page, we send you occasional news and event emails until you unsubscribe.
Who sees it

HAART volunteers who handle adoptions, fostering and fundraising. Our form submissions are stored in our content system and emailed to our inbox. We do not sell or trade personal information. We share it only with service providers who process it for us (email delivery, payment processing, content hosting) and where the law requires.
Analytics
This site uses Plausible Analytics, which does not use cookies and does not collect personal information. We can see how many people visit each page and which links they follow, not who they are.
Photographs

We publish photographs of animals in our care. We do not publish identifying information about people who surrender animals, and we do not publish details of cruelty cases that are under investigation.
Access and correction
Email info@haart.org.au to ask what we hold about you, to correct it, or to have it deleted where we no longer need it.
Complaints
Email us first. If you are not satisfied, you can complain to the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner at oaic.gov.au.
This policy was last updated on 17 September 2026.

A real story on this page would follow one animal from the day HAART took it on: where it came from, what the vet found, what the foster carer noticed in the first week, and where it is now.
